analysis:
All three changed files are documentation only, so no executable control changed in the supplied evidence. No findings.

1. docs/reference/configuration.md: the visible excerpt (head 502-580) is unchanged prefix-cache and benchmark rows. The patch excerpt, truncated at head lines 320-323, adds opt-in env vars DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_MTP, _DEPTH and _VERIFICATION. They are documented as default off and not forwarded to LaunchAgents, and MTP-speculating owners refuse media. The reader code (NemotronSuperLocalMTP.swift) was not supplied, so those claims are unverified. No relation to T-041 prefix-cache identity was reviewed; the numerical-env identity prefix list in ssd-kv-cache.md (DARKBLOOM_CBV2_, _QWEN_, _MTP_, etc.) does not obviously include DARKBLOOM_NEMOTRON_SUPER_*. Whether those toggles are bound into cache identity for that owner needs the code to confirm. It is only an open question, since the owner is described as unregistered.

2. docs/reference/nemotron-super-image-formats.md (new, head 1-100): documents an in-process PNG decoder and an ImageIO JPEG path that parse consumer-supplied (adversarial) inline images on the provider (A-001, T-050-adjacent). It states limits: 8 MiB body, pixel and axis caps, a 256 MiB resize workspace, a quote-based memory reservation, a 500-scan cap, and CRC, zlib and chunk-size checks. The decoder and binding sources (NemotronSuperImageDecode.swift, NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.swift) were not supplied. The next pass should check them if they appear in other batches, especially cancellation, since the doc admits ImageIO decode cannot be cancelled. The doc says the owner is unregistered, so there is no evidence of production exposure. The threat model has no entry for the new image-decoder attack surface (memory and DoS from hostile images). That is a possible documentation gap but not a regression shown here.

3. docs/reference/ssd-kv-cache.md line 186: adds the claim that a cold result returns only after its attempt's host IO refund completes. This only tightens the documentation of the resource-accounting claim. Retry bounds, TTL (1800 s) and DBK3 crypto/identity text are unchanged and consistent with T-041.
